env.name: cmv
env.description:
Measure the supplied hypotheses; do not discover, rewrite or refine them. Each feature is
one scalar measurement of a discussion row, not a separate observation for every comment.
The full supplied corpus contains 2,000 rows: 1,000 changed and 1,000 unchanged outcomes.
Describe associations, not proven causal effects or prospective prediction.

Columns:
  - post_created_utc: Unix timestamp for the original post, not a comment or score-measurement
    timestamp. Response delay cannot be calculated from it.
  - title: the original poster's (OP's) heading or claim statement, not the argument body.
  - argument: the OP's explanation of their view. Use this field for argument-body measurements;
    include title only when the requested scope includes the heading or when it is needed to
    interpret a comment's target. Text can contain quotations, edits and outcome announcements.
  - OC_comments: a JSON-encoded list of available counter-argument comments by OTHER users,
    not the OP. Parse the list before counting comments, words or semantic instances.
    Specify any/all/count/share/mean explicitly. List order is not rank, importance or chronology.
    If properties must coexist in one comment, assess their conjunction within that comment;
    separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. The row-level extractor still returns one scalar.
    List length counts comments, not necessarily distinct commenters. No per-comment outcomes,
    scores or timestamps are supplied. OP-language measurements use title/argument instead.
  - conversation: formatted interaction text overlapping OC_comments, not extra independent
    evidence. It may include later replies and explicit view-change announcements. Do not use
    it as an initial-argument snapshot. When interaction is required, specify speaker/turn
    selection and use it only if faithful measurement is possible under the leakage guard below.
  - log_length: a supplied log-transformed length measure. Construction, source text, log base
    and timing are undocumented. When named by the hypothesis, use the supplied value and state
    that limitation; do not equate it with argument word count or reconstruct its log base.
  - post_score: the observed original-post score, not a comment score, voter count or initial
    endorsement. Its measurement time relative to the outcome is unknown; post_created_utc
    does not establish that timing.
  - delta: OUTCOME, 1 if the OP changed their view, else 0. Never a predictor or annotation input.
  - post_id, comment_id: identifiers, never predictors.

Attribution and unavailable measurements:
  - No measured personality scores, Big Five questionnaires or author demographics are supplied.
    A personality inference from writing is a linguistic proxy, not an observed trait; do not
    substitute it silently when the hypothesis requires an unavailable measurement.
  - Distinguish the author's own assertions or experiences from attributed quotations.
    An external source cited as support can count for an evidence feature without making the
    source's wording or experience the author's own. Background/rebuttal quotations are not
    automatically adopted support. Apply this distinction to OP text and other users' comments.
    Quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker.

Predictor leakage guard (applies to every text field):
  - Never use the OP's own view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or
    resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred as predictor evidence.
    This exclusion applies even inside argument and even if such text expresses the construct.
    Generic discussion of platform/delta rules is not an outcome announcement; retain relevant
    discussion rather than blanket-removing mentions of delta.
  - Subject to this guard, measure supplied current text unless the hypothesis restricts time.
    Deleting marked edits or outcome announcements does not reconstruct initial/pre-outcome
    text. Neither post_created_utc nor unordered comments supplies missing comment/edit times.
    An edit marker alone does not establish when an edit occurred.
    If faithful exposure requires unavailable temporal information, state that limitation and
    set term=null; do not substitute current text or infer a snapshot.
  - delta remains the fixed outcome. A hypothesis requiring another outcome or outcome-reporting
    text as a predictor is unsupported: explain the limitation and set term=null.
    If excluding outcome evidence changes the requested predictor itself, preserve the original
    claim as unsupported; do not silently replace it with a cleaned concession/attitude proxy.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument includes explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms are associated with lower view change than those without such comparisons.

features.name: argument_compares_to_established_norms
features.definition: OP argument text: 1 if it makes an explicit comparison to established scientific or historical norms, else 0
features.spec: Read only the OP's argument column (current text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP's own argument explicitly compares the view, claim, case or situation under discussion to an established scientific norm (e.g., accepted scientific consensus, standard scientific practice/findings) or an established historical norm (e.g., historical precedent, long-standing historical standard or practice), with the comparison stated explicitly in the text. Return 0 if the argument has no such explicit comparison (mere mention of science or history without comparing to a norm does not count). Quotations of others count only if the OP adopts them as their own comparison. Ignore and do not use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is neither such an announcement nor positive evidence by itself. Missing or malformed argument: return null. Output a single 0/1 value.

decomposed.h0: There is no association between argument_compares_to_established_norms and delta (view change).
decomposed.h1: Rows with argument_compares_to_established_norms=1 are associated with lower view change (delta) than rows with 0.
decomposed.note: Measures current supplied argument text, including marked edits, not an initial snapshot; outcome announcements are excluded by the prompt. Association only, not causal. The measurement is semantic and "established norm" has no further operational boundary beyond the stated definition.

decomposed.hypothesis: Arguments expressing explicit fear of social rejection or isolation are associated with lower view-change rates than arguments stating beliefs without emotional self-defense.

features.name: op_fear_social_rejection
features.definition: OP's own title/argument text: 1 if the OP explicitly expresses fear of social rejection or isolation (e.g., being shunned, ostracized, disliked, left alone) in relation to holding or stating the view; else 0
features.spec: Read the OP's title and argument only. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly expresses fear, worry or dread of social rejection, ostracism, disapproval by others, or isolation/loneliness as a consequence of holding, voicing or abandoning the view. Return 0 if the text is assessable and has no such explicit expression. Exclude quoted or reported others' positions or feelings not adopted by the OP, and moderator/bot notices. Ignore and do not use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even inside the argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is neither outcome evidence nor a positive indicator by itself. Use supplied current text including marked edits (other than excluded outcome content); do not infer an initial snapshot. If title and argument are both missing or malformed, return null. Output 0 or 1.

features.name: op_other_emotional_self_defense
features.definition: OP's own title/argument text: 1 if the OP shows emotional self-defense (defensive protection of feelings or ego, e.g., preemptive hurt, anger or shielding) that is NOT fear of social rejection or isolation; else 0
features.spec: Read the OP's title and argument only. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, shows emotional self-defense, i.e. explicitly defends or shields their feelings, ego or identity against anticipated attack or hurt (e.g., preemptive defensiveness, pleas not to be attacked, emotional bracing), and the defense does NOT consist of explicit fear of social rejection or isolation. Return 0 if the text is assessable and contains no such emotional self-defense (including plain statements of belief with reasons) or only fear of social rejection/isolation. Exclude quoted or reported others' positions not adopted by the OP and moderator/bot notices. Ignore and do not use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even inside the argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not outcome evidence. Use supplied current text including marked edits (other than excluded outcome content); do not infer an initial snapshot. If title and argument are both missing or malformed, return null. Output 0 or 1.

decomposed.h0: Controlling for op_other_emotional_self_defense, the delta rate does not differ between rows with op_fear_social_rejection=1 and rows with neither feature (beta of op_fear_social_rejection = 0).
decomposed.h1: Rows with op_fear_social_rejection=1 have lower view-change rates than the reference group of rows with neither feature (beta of op_fear_social_rejection < 0).
decomposed.note: Reference group is rows with neither fear of rejection nor other emotional self-defense, operationalizing "stating beliefs without emotional self-defense"; the second feature keeps other self-defense rows from contaminating it. The claim is read as concerning the OP's argument text. Current text including edits is used after excluding outcome announcements; no initial snapshot is reconstructed. Association only; OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model. Rows may be rare for the fear feature.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that cite specific, functioning institutional precedents are associated with a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract normative principles.

features.name: any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent
features.definition: Other users' counter-argument comments: 1 if any comment cites a specific, functioning institutional precedent (a particular existing institution, policy, law or system presented as actually operating) as support, else 0
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP). Parse the list. Return 1 if at least one comment cites a specific institutional precedent that is presented as actually functioning/operating in practice (e.g. a named existing law, policy, organization, or system in some country or institution, and how it works), used as support for the comment's argument. Hypothetical institutions, purely abstract principles, and personal anecdotes that are not institutional do not qualify. Evidence need not be externally verified. Ignore any text reporting the OP's view change, delta awards, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates or whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement. Return 0 if the list is valid and nonempty but no comment qualifies, 0 for a valid empty list, and null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Output a single 0/1.

features.name: any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles
features.definition: Other users' counter-argument comments: 1 if any comment relies on abstract normative principles (general moral/value principles about what ought to be) as its argument, else 0
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP). Parse the list. Return 1 if at least one comment argues by relying on abstract normative principles, i.e. general moral, ethical or value principles about what should or ought to be (e.g. fairness, rights, autonomy, justice) stated in general terms rather than via a specific concrete case or institution. Ignore any text reporting the OP's view change, delta awards, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates or whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement. Return 0 if the list is valid and nonempty but no comment qualifies, 0 for a valid empty list, and null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Output a single 0/1.

decomposed.h0: Holding any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles fixed, the association of any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent with delta equals that of any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles (equal coefficients).
decomposed.h1: any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent is associated with a higher probability of delta than any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles (coefficient of precedent greater than that of abstract principles).
decomposed.note: The claim is a contrast between precedent-citing and abstract-principle comments (beta_A - beta_B), which no single design-matrix coefficient represents; testing beta_A alone would compare with neither-type rows, so term=null. The features are not mutually exclusive (a row can have both). Comment order is unknown; features are row-level any-indicators over current text. Associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring longer precomputed log-transformed discussion length are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: supplied_log_length
features.definition: Supplied precomputed log-transformed discussion length value for the row, used as given
features.spec: Return pd.to_numeric(df['log_length'], errors='coerce') per row; null if missing or non-numeric. Use the supplied value as is (observed range about 0.69-7.44); do not recompute, rescale, or reconstruct the log base.

decomposed.h0: supplied_log_length has no association with the likelihood of delta (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Higher supplied_log_length is associated with a higher likelihood of delta (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: log_length construction, source text, log base and timing relative to the outcome are undocumented; it may include post-outcome text, and it is not equated with word count. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit admissions of uncertainty are associated with a higher probability of view change than those asserting absolute certainty.

features.name: op_admits_uncertainty
features.definition: OP argument text (OP's own voice): 1 if it contains an explicit admission of uncertainty or possible error about the OP's own view/claims, else 0
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's own text, current supplied text including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly admits uncertainty, doubt or possible error about their own view or claims (e.g. 'I'm not sure', 'I might be wrong', 'I could be mistaken', 'I'm unsure'). Do not count inviting critique alone, generic hedging unrelated to the OP's own view's certainty, or uncertainty expressed only in quoted/reported text from others unless the OP adopts it. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates or text reporting whether the outcome occurred (e.g. 'EDIT: my view was changed', 'delta awarded'); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an announcement and remains eligible. Return 0 if the text is assessable and contains no such admission; return null if argument is missing or empty/malformed. Output one value: 0, 1 or null.

features.name: op_asserts_absolute_certainty
features.definition: OP argument text (OP's own voice): 1 if it explicitly asserts absolute certainty about the OP's own view, else 0
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's own text, current supplied text including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly asserts absolute certainty about their view or claims (e.g. 'I am 100% certain', 'there is no possible way I'm wrong', 'undeniably', 'absolutely certain nothing could change my mind'). Ordinary confident claims or strong opinion without an explicit assertion of absolute certainty do not count; quoted or reported others' certainty does not count unless the OP adopts it. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an announcement and remains eligible. Return 0 if assessable and no such assertion; null if argument is missing or empty/malformed. Output one value: 0, 1 or null.

decomposed.h0: Discussions whose argument has op_admits_uncertainty=1 have the same probability of view change as those with op_asserts_absolute_certainty=1.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with op_admits_uncertainty=1 have a higher probability of view change than those with op_asserts_absolute_certainty=1.
decomposed.note: Claim is a contrast between named groups (uncertainty admission vs absolute certainty), i.e. beta_uncertainty - beta_certainty; neither single coefficient in the model (each is relative to the neither/baseline group, and groups can overlap) represents it, so term=null. Measured on current supplied argument text including edits, after excluding outcome-reporting content; no initial snapshot is reconstructed. Absolute certainty is likely rare; no frequency cutoff is imposed. Associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently challenging multiple distinct factual premises within the argument are positively associated with view change.

features.name: distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments, other users) read against the OP title/argument: number of distinct factual premises stated in the OP argument that are challenged by at least one comment
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to identify the OP's factual premises (empirical/factual claims the OP's argument relies on; not purely value judgments). Count the number of DISTINCT factual premises of the OP argument that are explicitly challenged (disputed as false, inaccurate, unsupported by facts, or contradicted with evidence) by at least one comment. Deduplicate: the same premise challenged by several comments counts once; different premises challenged in one comment count separately. Do not count challenges to values, logic only, or to non-premises, and do not count agreement or merely tangential remarks. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if in the argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is neither counted as a challenge nor excluded as context. Use current supplied text; list order implies no rank or chronology. Output a non-negative integer. 0 = no factual premise challenged. If OC_comments is a valid empty list return 0. If OC_comments, title or argument is missing/malformed so the measurement cannot be assessed, return null.

features.name: challenges_multiple_distinct_factual_premises
features.definition: Counter-arguments challenge at least two distinct factual premises of the OP argument (1) else 0
features.spec: Using `distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count`: return null if df['distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count'] is null; else return 1 if df['distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count'] >= 2, else 0.

decomposed.h0: challenges_multiple_distinct_factual_premises has no association with delta.
decomposed.h1: challenges_multiple_distinct_factual_premises is positively associated with delta.
decomposed.note: "Frequently" has no specified cutoff; operationalized only via "multiple" = at least two distinct premises (count >= 2), pooled across the row's comments (distinct count, not comment count). This threshold is the operational reading of "multiple", not a frequency rule. The count is available as a separate feature. Comment order/time unknown; current text used with outcome announcements excluded. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: counter_argument_comment_count
features.definition: Count of available counter-argument comments by other users in the row's OC_comments list
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings. Return len(list). Empty valid list -> 0; missing or malformed (unparseable or non-list) -> null. No semantic filtering; every list element counts as one comment. Equivalent: df['OC_comments'].apply(lambda s: len(json.loads(s))).

decomposed.h0: counter_argument_comment_count has no association with the likelihood of delta (OP view change).
decomposed.h1: Higher counter_argument_comment_count (more counter-argument responses) is associated with a higher likelihood of delta; fewer with lower.
decomposed.note: Hypothesis wording ("original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses") is interpreted as the number of available counter-argument comments in OC_comments for the discussion. Count is of the supplied list only (observed min 1, so no empty lists); it may not be the full set of responses, is not distinct commenters, and has no chronology. Association only, linear OLS on delta; no causal claim.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions with at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: distinct_counterargument_count
features.definition: Other users' comments in OC_comments: count of distinct counter-arguments (semantically deduplicated) against the OP's view
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP), parsing the list first; use title and argument only to identify the OP's view that is being countered. Count the number of distinct counter-arguments the comments present against the OP's view. Semantically deduplicate: the same argument repeated in several comments counts once; one comment may contain several distinct counter-arguments, each counted. Do not count mere questions, agreement with the OP, jokes, or moderator/bot notices. Ignore list order. Exclude any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if in argument or comments; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an announcement and stays eligible but is not itself a counter-argument unless it argues against the OP's view. Use current supplied text as given. Output a non-negative integer. A valid empty comment list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null; if OP context is missing so that the target view cannot be determined, give null. 0 means no counter-argument is present.

features.name: has_at_least_three_distinct_counterarguments
features.definition: Row has at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments (threshold on the distinct counter-argument count)
features.spec: Using `distinct_counterargument_count`: return null if df['distinct_counterargument_count'] is null, else 1 if df['distinct_counterargument_count'] >= 3, else 0.

decomposed.h0: has_at_least_three_distinct_counterarguments has no association with the likelihood of delta (OP view change).
decomposed.h1: Rows with has_at_least_three_distinct_counterarguments = 1 have a higher likelihood of delta than rows with 0.
decomposed.note: Association only, not causal. Counts are over the supplied available comments (OC_comments), which may not be the full discussion; the list is unordered and comments may not be from distinct commenters. Distinctness is a semantic judgment of the annotator. Threshold of 3 comes from the hypothesis. Comment and edit timing is unavailable; current text is used after outcome-leakage exclusion. Linear probability model via OLS.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post title uses absolute certainty markers are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: title_absolute_certainty
features.definition: OP title: 1 if the title uses absolute certainty markers (e.g., universal/total claims or language asserting no possible doubt or exception), else 0
features.spec: Read only the title column (the OP's heading). Return 1 if the title uses absolute certainty markers, i.e. wording that presents the claim as certain, universal, or exceptionless with no room for doubt (e.g. 'all', 'never', 'always', 'every', 'definitely', 'undeniably', 'no one', 'impossible', 'obviously'); these are illustrative, not exhaustive, and the judgment is semantic about the title's own assertion. Return 0 if the title has no such markers (including hedged or merely opinionated titles). Ignore the generic 'CMV:' prefix. Exclude any text in the title that announces a view change or delta award, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or reports of outcome; such text is not evidence (generic mentions of delta/platform rules may be retained but are not certainty markers by themselves). Do not use other columns. If title is missing or empty, return null.

decomposed.h0: title_absolute_certainty has no association with the likelihood that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with title_absolute_certainty = 1 are associated with a lower likelihood of delta than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Association only, not causal. The title is current supplied text; its time of writing relative to any edits is unknown. "Absolute certainty markers" has no fixed lexicon; the illustrative terms are non-exhaustive and the semantic judgment is an operational assumption.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where original posts explicitly invite critique or use tentative language are associated with higher view-change rates than those using absolute, definitive declarations.

features.name: op_invites_critique_or_tentative
features.definition: OP title and argument (OP's own voice): 1 if the OP explicitly invites critique/challenge to their view OR uses tentative/hedged language about their own view, else 0
features.spec: Read title and argument (the OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly invites critique, counterarguments or challenge to their view (e.g. 'change my view', 'convince me otherwise', 'tell me where I'm wrong') OR expresses their own view in tentative/hedged terms (e.g. 'I think maybe', 'I'm not sure', 'I could be wrong', 'it seems to me'). Return 0 if neither is present. Ignore quoted external text or others' positions not adopted by the OP. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered. Use current supplied text including marked edits (other than excluded outcome text); do not infer an initial snapshot. If both title and argument are missing or empty, return null.

features.name: op_uses_absolute_declarations
features.definition: OP title and argument (OP's own voice): 1 if the OP states their own view in absolute/definitive declarations (certainty, no hedging or qualification), else 0
features.spec: Read title and argument (the OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, states their central view using absolute, definitive declarations expressing certainty (e.g. 'always', 'never', 'obviously', 'undeniably', 'there is no way', 'this is simply a fact') without hedging. Return 0 if no such absolute declarations are present. Ignore quoted external text or others' positions not adopted by the OP. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered. Use current supplied text including marked edits (other than excluded outcome text); do not infer an initial snapshot. If both title and argument are missing or empty, return null.

decomposed.h0: Discussion rows with op_invites_critique_or_tentative do not differ in view-change rate from rows with op_uses_absolute_declarations.
decomposed.h1: Rows with op_invites_critique_or_tentative have higher view-change rates than rows with op_uses_absolute_declarations.
decomposed.note: The claim compares two named groups (invite/tentative vs absolute/definitive). The features are not complements and can overlap or both be 0, and no single OLS coefficient equals the difference between the two groups, so term=null. Each coefficient is relative to rows with neither feature, not to the other group. Text is current supplied text including edits, with outcome announcements excluded by the prompt. No initial snapshot is reconstructed. Results would be associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that explicitly cite specific real-world examples are associated with higher likelihood of original view change.

features.name: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example
features.definition: Any OC_comments counter-argument comment (by other users): explicitly cites at least one specific real-world example (actual case, event, person, institution, or concrete personal experience) as part of its argument
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP). Parse the list. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly cites a specific real-world example, i.e. a concrete actual case, event, person, organization, study/instance, or specific personal experience that actually occurred, used in its argument. Invented or hypothetical scenarios, vague generalities with no specific case, and purely abstract reasoning do not count. Endorsement by the OP is not needed; examples need not be of any particular type and no outside verification is required. Ignore any text that is an OP view-change or delta-award announcement, post-outcome thank-you/resolution update, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; such text is not evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered but is not itself a real-world example unless it is a specific case. Use current supplied text only; list order carries no meaning. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including a valid empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example has no association with the likelihood of delta (view change).
decomposed.h1: Rows with any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example = 1 are associated with a higher likelihood of delta.
decomposed.note: Hypothesis wording "discussions featuring counter-arguments that cite..." is operationalized as any comment (not share/count). Association only, not causal. Current OC_comments text is used; comment timing is unavailable. OLS on a binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counterarguments containing measured, logical reasoning are positively associated with the original poster changing their mind compared to those containing emotional aggression in ChangeMyView discussions.

features.name: any_comment_measured_logical_reasoning
features.definition: Other users' counter-argument comments (OC_comments): 1 if any comment presents measured, logical reasoning (calm, reasoned argument with premises supporting conclusions), else 0
features.spec: Read only OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP). Parse the list. Return 1 if at least one comment contains measured, logical reasoning: a calm, even-toned argument that supports its claims with reasons or inference steps. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment does. Empty valid list -> 0. Missing or malformed input -> null. A comment may also be aggressive; judge only whether it contains measured logical reasoning. List order carries no meaning. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; do not use them as evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered. Output 0/1 or null.

features.name: any_comment_emotional_aggression
features.definition: Other users' counter-argument comments (OC_comments): 1 if any comment contains emotional aggression (hostile, insulting, angry or contemptuous attack), else 0
features.spec: Read only OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP). Parse the list. Return 1 if at least one comment contains emotional aggression: hostile, angry, insulting, contemptuous or belittling language aimed at the OP or their view. Mere disagreement, blunt or generic emotional wording without hostility is not aggression. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment does. Empty valid list -> 0. Missing or malformed input -> null. List order carries no meaning. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; do not use them as evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered. Output 0/1 or null.

decomposed.h0: Rows with any_comment_measured_logical_reasoning have the same association with delta as rows with any_comment_emotional_aggression (beta_logical = beta_aggression).
decomposed.h1: any_comment_measured_logical_reasoning is more positively associated with delta than any_comment_emotional_aggression (beta_logical > beta_aggression).
decomposed.note: The claim is a contrast between logical reasoning and emotional aggression. No single design-matrix coefficient represents beta_logical - beta_aggression, so term is null. Neither coefficient alone tests the comparison. The features are row-level any-indicators, and the two can overlap within a row. Comment-level comparison and list order are not available. Associations only, not causal. Current text is used, with outcome announcements excluded.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote and refute specific factual claims in the original post are associated with higher rates of view change.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim

Return 1 if every comment rebuts the OP's claim using abstract, general or theoretical reasoning (principles, logic, general arguments, concepts) and no comment contains a concrete personal anecdote (the commenter's own specific experience or that of someone they know). Return 0 if at least one comment contains a concrete personal anecdote, or any comment is not an abstract theoretical rebuttal (e.g. relies on non-personal concrete case or data instead). Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, including inside argument; generic delta/platform rule discussion is neither evidence nor excluded by itself. No single design-matrix column represents that difference (each coefficient is relative to the omitted mixed/other group), so term=null. The features are mutually exclusive by construction. Current text is used, with outcome-reporting text excluded; comment order and timing are unavailable. "Abstract theoretical" and "concrete personal anecdote" are operational interpretations.
